use_case_name: Copy Uncompressed Files to Another Location

claims.content: To allow the user to copy selected files or folders from one location to another within the file system using PeaZip’s file management interface.

goal.raw_text: To allow the user to copy selected files or folders from one location to another within the file system using PeaZip’s file management interface.

claims.content: User
The user is running the PeaZip application.
The user has navigated to the source location containing the files or folders to be copied using the File Manager Interface.
The user has selected the specific object(s) (files or folders) intended for copying.
The user drags an archived object (file or archive) from PeaZip to a location on the computer system.

trigger.raw_text: The user drags an archived object (file or archive) from PeaZip to a location on the computer system.

claims.content: The user selects the file(s) or folder(s) to be copied in the File Manager Interface.
The user initiates the copy action by pressing Ctrl+C, as listed under 'Modify' operations for selected objects.
The user navigates to the destination location using the File Manager Interface (e.g., via browsing computer system locations, up one level, or going back/forward in history).
The user pastes the copied object(s) into the destination location by pressing Ctrl+V, as listed under 'Modify' operations.
The user cancels the current selection and clears the clipboard by pressing Esc, as listed under 'Modify' operations.
The user performs a quick delete or secure delete on selected objects instead of copying, using Del or Shift+Del respectively, as listed under 'Modify' operations.
The user cuts the selected object(s) using Ctrl+X instead of copying, then pastes them to move rather than duplicate, as listed under 'Modify' operations.
The selected file(s) or folder(s) are successfully duplicated in the destination location.
The original files remain unchanged at their source location.
The clipboard is cleared after the paste operation completes, unless explicitly canceled by the user via Esc.
